connections.why: Both apply the language levels to describe how English varies
Regional variation is one dimension of individual difference
Gender identity is a social factor shaping individual language
Historical spread of English produced today's global varieties
Children's developing speech is analysed with the same toolkit
Spoken skills feed into the later move to writing
Power and status are key drivers of language choice
Journalism exercises influential power through bias and framing
Both study variation across communities of English speakers
Gendered language often reflects unequal power relationships
Understanding variation lets students craft for audience and function
Genre study models the writing students produce in coursework
The commentary reflects on the choices made while writing
Acquisition theory and change both trace how language develops
